squawks.headline: Dutch Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q, above 0.3% forecast; annual growth picks up to 2.1%
squawks.detail: Preliminary figures show Dutch GDP grew 0.6% q/q in the third quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and matching the previous quarter's 0.6%. Annual growth came in at 2.1%, compared with a forecast of 1.3% and 1.6% previously.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says he is working to end the Iran war quickly, citing its heavy impact on Europe
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the Iran war is having a major impact on Europe and that this is why he is holding intensive talks on his Asia trip. He also said the US is shifting its foreign policy and Germany must do likewise.

squawks.headline: Spanish Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q in line with forecast, slowing from 0.7%; annual growth picks up to 2.7%
squawks.detail: Spain's preliminary third-quarter estimate shows 0.6% growth on the quarter, as forecast and down from 0.7% previously. Annual growth is 2.7%, matching the forecast and up from 2.6%.

squawks.headline: Spanish flash October national CPI holds at 4.9% y/y as forecast; monthly rise of 0.6% is below the 0.7% forecast
squawks.detail: Spain's flash national CPI for October is unchanged at 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast. On the month, prices rise 0.6%, against a 0.7% forecast and 0.3% previously.

squawks.headline: Spanish flash October HICP eases to 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast and down from 5.0%; up 0.5% m/m
squawks.detail: Spain's flash October HICP rose 4.9% y/y, matching the 4.9% forecast, after 5.0% the month before. On the month it rose 0.5%, also in line with forecast, after 0.6% previously.

squawks.headline: ECB's Dolenc says the energy shock is not yet feeding broader price pressures but warns inflation may stay above 2% for years
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Dolenc said the energy shock had not yet spread into wider price pressures, but that higher energy prices risk more persistent inflation. He added that inflation could remain above 2% in the coming years.

squawks.headline: French flash October HICP rises 3.8% y/y, above 3.6% forecast and up from 3.4% in September
squawks.detail: France's preliminary October harmonised inflation came in at 3.8% y/y and 0.4% m/m, against forecasts of 3.6% and 0.3%. National CPI rose 3.4% y/y against a 3.3% forecast (previously 3.1%), and 0.4% m/m against a 0.2% forecast (previously -0.3%).

squawks.headline: French producer prices rise 1.7% m/m in September, up from 1.0% the previous month
squawks.detail: French PPI rose 1.7% month on month, compared with 1.0% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the BoJ is watching spring wage talks closely, which must make 2% inflation built in
squawks.detail: Speaking after the BoJ's policy decision, Governor Ueda said the bank is watching next spring's wage negotiations closely and that annual wage talks need to reach a point where 2% inflation is built in. He added that the BoJ still needs to watch whether the price trend becomes anchored.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the policy rate is still below neutral and will be adjusted at the right time to stop risks materialising
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said at his post-decision press conference that work remains because the policy rate is below the neutral level. He also said rate adjustments would be timed to prevent risks from materialising.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says he wants to bring the policy rate to a neutral level in an appropriate way
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said this at his press conference after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda expects faster ETF sales to have only a limited market impact; says upside risks need an appropriate response
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda spoke after the decision to speed up ETF sales. He said the faster pace should have only a limited effect on markets and that the bank must respond appropriately to upside risks.

squawks.headline: China's most-active 30-year government bond futures contract drops 1.00% intraday to 117.34 yuan
squawks.detail: The most-active TL contract on 30-year Chinese government bonds fell 1.00% during the session to 117.34 yuan.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says a rate rise will be considered at every meeting, the next one included
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank will weigh a rate increase at each policy meeting, including the next one. He spoke after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

squawks.headline: Nationwide UK house prices flat m/m in October against -0.2% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.5%
squawks.detail: Nationwide's October index shows UK house prices unchanged on the month, after -0.2% in September, against a -0.2% forecast. Annual growth (NSA) eases to 0.5% from 0.8%, below the 0.6% forecast.

squawks.headline: German import prices rise 10.4% y/y in September, above 10.3% forecast; up 2.1% m/m
squawks.detail: German import prices rose 10.4% from a year earlier, against a 10.3% forecast and 8.3% previously. On the month they rose 2.1%, against a 2% forecast and 1.0% previously.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says inflation expectations remain only weakly anchored around 2%; declines to discuss revising government accord
squawks.detail: At his post-decision news conference, BoJ Governor Ueda said inflation expectations are still weakly anchored around 2%. He would not say whether the accord between the BoJ and the government needs revising.

squawks.headline: French finance minister Lescure says economy has stalled in 2026 and calls for a budget to support confidence
squawks.detail: France's finance minister said the economy came to a standstill in 2026 and that the country needs a budget to boost confidence and growth. His remarks came after preliminary Q3 GDP data showed a contraction.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda stops short of declaring the 2% inflation target met; sees overshoot risks little changed from a month ago
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, the Bank of Japan Governor said inflation must sit stably and sustainably around 2% before the target is deemed met, and that the BoJ will not make a formal announcement when it is achieved. He added that the risk of inflation exceeding the target is not significantly higher than a month ago, and that whether wage growth is sustainable remains an important consideration.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says economic and inflation trends will be examined at each meeting, with closer monitoring of risks
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said policymakers will check the data to judge whether underlying inflation is stable and will assess how well inflation expectations align with the 2% target. He added that economic and financial risks need closer monitoring to guide policy.

squawks.headline: Poll: 27 of 29 economists say a 4.85% RBA cash rate will be the peak for the year
squawks.detail: A poll of economists finds 27 of 29 expect an RBA cash rate of 4.85% to mark the high point for the year.

squawks.headline: 30 of 32 economists in a poll expect the RBA to raise its cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November
squawks.detail: In a poll of economists, 30 of the 32 surveyed said the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise its cash rate to 4.85% at its 3 November decision.

squawks.headline: Ueda says BoJ will keep raising its policy rate as activity, prices and financial conditions evolve; credits government measures
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said government measures had boosted economic activity and helped bring the 2% price goal within reach. He also said core CPI inflation is broadly in line with the 2% target and is expected to stay near that level.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation is near the 2% goal and financial conditions remain accommodative; flags FX, AI and Middle East risks
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said rates will rise further depending on economic, inflation and financial conditions, and that policy adjustments depend on outlook risks. He also said the BoJ will keep J-REIT sales at the current pace.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda expects Japan's economy to keep growing moderately; puts mid- to long-term inflation expectations at around 2%
squawks.detail: The BoJ Governor made the remarks after the bank kept its short-term rate at 1.25%. He said medium- to long-term inflation expectations are around 2%.

squawks.headline: French GDP falls 0.1% y/y in preliminary Q3 estimate against 0.3% forecast; September consumer spending down 0.4% y/y
squawks.detail: The annual GDP figure compares with growth of 0.5% in the previous quarter. Consumer spending fell 0.4% y/y in September, against a forecast rise of 0.4% and a previous reading of 0.8%.

squawks.headline: French GDP shrinks 0.1% q/q in preliminary Q3 estimate, below 0.1% forecast; consumer spending falls 0.5% m/m
squawks.detail: Preliminary French GDP fell 0.1% q/q against a forecast rise of 0.1% and 0.0% previously, and was down 0.1% y/y against a forecast 0.3% and 0.5% previously. Consumer spending fell 0.5% m/m against a forecast rise of 0.1%, matching the previous -0.5%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Simkus says risk of energy spillover has risen but second-round effects are not yet visible
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Simkus said the likelihood of energy prices spilling over into wider inflation has increased. He added that second-round effects are not yet visible.

squawks.headline: Sterling moves above $1.3350 in early trade
squawks.detail: A market report said sterling rose past 1.3350 against the dollar but stayed below its 100-day moving average.

squawks.headline: Japan's 20-year JGB yield falls 6.5bp to 3.605% after BoJ decision
squawks.detail: The 20-year Japanese government bond yield dropped 6.5bp to 3.605% following the Bank of Japan's decision to hold rates. Market reports also said the yen strengthened and the Nikkei fell further after the decision.

squawks.headline: BoJ raises its inflation forecast while keeping rates on hold
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the Bank of Japan revised up its inflation forecast on Friday and said again that it was ready to keep raising borrowing costs to head off growing inflation risks.

squawks.headline: Yen firms and 5-year JGB yield falls 3.5bp to 2.235% after BoJ hold described as hawkish
squawks.detail: The yen strengthened against the dollar after the Bank of Japan's decision, which market commentary called a hawkish pause, as attention moved to Governor Ueda. 10-year JGB futures gave back some earlier gains but were still up 0.34 point, and the 5-year JGB yield fell 3.5bp to 2.235%.

squawks.headline: Japan finance minister Katayama expects BoJ to work closely with government to reach 2% inflation target
squawks.detail: Japan's finance minister Katayama said she expects the Bank of Japan to keep coordinating closely with the government on the 2% inflation target. She declined to comment on the day's BoJ decision.

squawks.headline: BoJ says it will keep raising rates if conditions allow; estimates proposed food tax cut would lower fiscal 2027 core CPI by 1.3pp
squawks.detail: Alongside its hold, the Bank of Japan said further rate rises would depend on how the economy and prices develop and named Middle East tensions, AI demand and currency swings as risks. Its projections leave out the proposed food consumption tax cut, which it estimates would lower fiscal 2027 core CPI by 1.3 percentage points and core-core CPI by 1.4 points.

squawks.headline: BoJ will speed up ETF sales to about 860bn yen a year from about 330bn yen, starting January 2027
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan says the new pace would take about 43 years to run down its ETF holdings, compared with about 112 years before. With its rate hold, the BoJ also says Japan now faces a risk of inflation overshooting, and that it will weigh the timing and pace of rate rises; dollar/yen was last down 0.37% at 157.115.

squawks.headline: BoJ holds short-term rate at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote; Takata dissents in favour of a rise to 1.5%
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan said underlying inflation is in line with its target, risks to prices are tilted to the upside and it will keep raising rates. Board medians are 2.5% for fiscal 2026 core CPI, 2.7% for fiscal 2027 core-core CPI and 0.7% for fiscal 2026 real GDP growth.

squawks.headline: Bonds head for their largest monthly gain in nearly three years as Asian tech shares slump on AI spending worries
squawks.detail: Reuters says investors moved into safe havens on Friday, with the yen rising and tech stocks falling on worries about returns on AI spending. Japan's 5-year JGB yield fell 5bp to 2.220%, the Nikkei dropped 3% and Taiwan's Taiex 3.5%.

squawks.headline: Brent and WTI rise $2 a barrel on growing US-Iran geopolitical risk
squawks.detail: Market reports say crude rebounded in Asian trade as doubts grew over the prospects of a peace deal, with both Brent and WTI up $2 a barrel.

squawks.headline: Sterling rises in Asian trade on a hawkish BoE outlook and broad dollar weakness
squawks.detail: A market report says sterling gained on expectations of a hawkish Bank of England and a broadly weaker US dollar; no levels were given.

squawks.headline: Japanese government bond yields slide, with 10-year at 2.775% and 20-year at 3.620%, ahead of BoJ
squawks.detail: The 10-year JGB yield slid to 2.775% and the 20-year to 3.620% in Asian trading as traders waited for the Bank of Japan decision.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields fall to seven-week lows as market odds of a December Fed hike ease to 70%
squawks.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 8.5bp to a seven-week low, and the 2-year yield fell further to 4.5648%, also a seven-week low, in Asian trading. Fed funds futures gained as the implied odds of a December rate rise eased to 70%.

squawks.headline: Australia Q3 producer prices rise 1.1% q/q, down from 1.3%; September private credit up 0.6%
squawks.detail: Australian producer prices rose 1.1% quarter on quarter in Q3, down from 1.3%, and the annual rate held at 3.6%. Private-sector credit rose 0.6% m/m in September against a 0.5% forecast, with housing credit up 0.4%, according to the central bank.

squawks.headline: Ukraine pauses strikes on Russian oil refineries after US pressure, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports, citing people with knowledge of the operations, that Ukraine's military has paused strikes on Russian refineries after pressure from President Trump. The pause is expected to last until after the US midterm elections and possibly further into November.

squawks.headline: LGA publishes briefing on the local government measures in the 28 October Autumn Budget
squawks.detail: The Local Government Association has released a briefing that summarises the Budget announcements relevant to councils and gives its initial view. The Chancellor delivered the Budget on 28 October 2026.

squawks.headline: US Q3 GDP growth is the fastest in a year; September PCE inflation rises 0.5%, the largest monthly gain in six months
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that US GDP expanded in the third quarter at its quickest pace in a year. September PCE inflation rose 0.5% on the month, the biggest increase in six months.

squawks.headline: US bonds rally as a tech share selloff drives broad rotation across markets
squawks.detail: A US market wrap reports that bonds rallied on Thursday as a selloff in technology stocks set off a wider rotation. No yield figures were given.

squawks.headline: Greek PM backs continued sanctions on Russia; says Greek shipowners would resume Black Sea trade if safe passage is assured
squawks.detail: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis restated his support for economic sanctions on Russia. He also said Greek shipowners are ready to resume Black Sea trading if safe passage is guaranteed, and urged the EU to send more naval assets to its Aspides mission in the Red Sea.

squawks.headline: US Energy Department awards contracts to exchange more than 40m barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
squawks.detail: The US Department of Energy said in a statement that it has awarded contracts for an exchange of more than 40m barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

squawks.headline: US Energy Department says companies will borrow 16.75m barrels of crude from the SPR out of 17m offered
squawks.detail: The US Energy Department said five companies, including Trafigura, Gunvor and Vitol, are taking loans of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. They will borrow 16.75 million of the 17 million barrels offered.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they hit Aramco's Abqaiq site and the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries; Saudi Arabia has not yet confirmed
squawks.detail: In statements, Yemen's Houthis said they attacked an Aramco facility at Abqaiq, the Ras Tanura and Rabigh oil refineries, and King Khalid airport in Riyadh and King Fahd airport in Dammam. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation, and no market reaction has been reported.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim several separate military operations deep inside Saudi territory
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi movement says it has carried out a number of distinct military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. This follows earlier Iranian media reports of Houthi missile attacks aimed at Saudi Aramco.

squawks.headline: Top US Middle East commander briefs Trump in person on Iran military options as US weighs resuming major combat, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials and others with direct knowledge, says the commander briefed Trump at the White House on Thursday. The report describes the in-person visit as rare.

squawks.headline: Think-tanks question whether Chancellor Healey's Budget deficit-reduction pledge is credible, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that leading think-tanks see the pledge to cut the deficit as unlikely to be met. They point to pressures on public services and households.

squawks.headline: Trump says Canada has been treating the US very well lately, amid the two countries' tariff dispute
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US President Trump told a rally on Thursday that Canada has recently been treating the US very nicely. The US has been in a tariff war with Canada.

squawks.headline: US is planning to strike Iran after next week's elections, Newsmax reports, citing officials
squawks.detail: Newsmax, citing unnamed officials, reports that the US plans strikes on Iran after next week's US elections. The batch gives no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Reuters says Chancellor Healey's first Budget passes with little market reaction, though some details leaked beforehand
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that markets barely moved on Chancellor John Healey's first Budget. It contrasts this with the leaks, U-turns and bond market jitters seen around earlier budgets, while noting that this one was not entirely free of leaks.

squawks.headline: Trump pledges $5,000 payment to every adult US citizen if Republicans win the House and Senate, at a cost of about $1tn
squawks.detail: Trump puts the cost of the proposed $5,000 payment at about $1 trillion and says tariff revenue would help pay for it. He says recipients would have to spend the payments in the US.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is working with Venezuela to produce millions of barrels of oil for the US
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US is working with Venezuela on oil production for the US, citing millions of barrels. He gave no timetable or further detail.

squawks.headline: Centre for Social Justice says a £33bn rise in UK benefits spending from 2027 to 2032 would offset frozen tax threshold gains
squawks.detail: Analysis by the Centre for Social Justice, reported by City AM, finds that the £33bn increase in benefits spending between 2027 and 2032 would broadly match the rise in projected receipts from frozen income tax thresholds.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US had to strike Iran to stop it obtaining a nuclear weapon
squawks.detail: US President Trump said military action against Iran was needed to prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says US military operations against Iran are going very well and repeats that the conflict will end very soon
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on 29 October. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia is ready for war but does not want one, and backs steps to restore relations with European countries
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin was speaking about his call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, who he said had made clear they were not representing the EU. He also said there would be no winners if things went too far, and that Russia does not want a Strait of Hormuz-type situation to arise in the Baltic Sea.

squawks.headline: Dallas Fed trimmed mean PCE inflation rises to 2.8% annualised in September from 2.0% in August
squawks.detail: The Dallas Fed's trimmed mean PCE price index rose at a 2.8% annualised rate in September, compared with 2.0% in August.

squawks.headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says talks can progress only once mediators accept Iran's seven conditions
squawks.detail: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran has set out its conditions to mediators many times and that pressure combined with incentives will not work on Iran. He said progress depends on all seven conditions being agreed.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Federal Reserve is reluctant to cut interest rates
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the Fed dislikes cutting interest rates, according to a market headline. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence lifts danger alerts for Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence said the danger had passed in Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran. It had issued the alerts earlier, after reports of Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Aramco.

squawks.headline: Iranian media report Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Aramco
squawks.detail: Fars News reported that Yemen's Houthi-run army had targeted Saudi Aramco in a broad wave of missile attacks, and other Iranian outlets carried similar reports. Saudi civil defence separately said the danger had passed in Najran city.

squawks.headline: US $44bn 7-year note auction stops on the screws at 4.894%, with bid-to-cover at 2.46
squawks.detail: The high yield of 4.894% matched the when-issued level, against 5.085% at the previous auction, and bid-to-cover rose from 2.420. Indirect bidders took 57.77%, direct bidders 32.82% and primary dealers 9.41%.

squawks.headline: UK welfare bill will not fall during this parliament, according to a market headline
squawks.detail: A market news feed reported at 17:00 GMT that the UK welfare bill will not come down this parliament; the post did not name a source. Earlier, ministers said the welfare bill needs to fall.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence issues danger alerts for Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority warned of potential danger in Najran, then in Riyadh and Al Kharj, in two alerts minutes apart. It gave no details of the threat, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Federal Reserve bids for US 7-year notes come to $4.9bn
squawks.detail: A market news account reported that the Federal Reserve's bids for US 7-year notes came to $4.9bn.

squawks.headline: EU states reaffirm accelerated release of 42.6 million barrels of oil stocks, half of it diesel, says Commissioner Jorgensen
squawks.detail: EU Energy Commissioner Jorgensen says member states have recommitted to an accelerated release of 42.6 million barrels from oil stocks, and half of the releases in the coming months will be diesel. He says the EU does not expect problems with oil and gas supply security but that citizens are struggling to pay their bills.

squawks.headline: UK public's year-ahead inflation expectations fall to 4.2% in October from 4.5%, Citi/YouGov survey shows
squawks.detail: The Citi/YouGov survey shows the public's year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.2% in October, down from 4.5% in September. Citi economists said there was no obvious explanation for the fall and that they were wary of reading it as more than normal volatility.

squawks.headline: UK public's long-term inflation expectations ease to 4.0% in October from 4.3%, Citi/YouGov survey shows
squawks.detail: The Citi/YouGov survey puts the UK public's long-term inflation expectations at 4.0% in October, down from 4.3% in September.

squawks.headline: Japan to start scaling back gasoline subsidies from December, PM Takaichi says
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the government will raise its target pump price for gasoline by 5 yen per litre each month from December into the spring. She said the aim is to contain the growing cost of fuel oil subsidies, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: US and Hungary sign a pipeline framework agreement, Hungary's foreign minister says
squawks.detail: Hungary's foreign minister said the US and Hungary have signed an agreement on what is being called the 'Trump Peace Pipeline Framework'. No further terms were given.

squawks.headline: Russia is set to extend its diesel export ban to the end of the year, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources say Russia is preparing to keep its ban on diesel exports in place until the end of the year. The report gives no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Trump says Vance's outreach to Iran was about helping it obtain medical supplies
squawks.detail: US President Trump says Vice President Vance's contact with Iran was about medical supplies, Reuters reports. US media had reported that Vance wrote to Iran's top security official to revive peace talks.

squawks.headline: US 4-week bill auction sells $115bn at 3.91% high yield, with bid-to-cover at 3.1
squawks.detail: The US Treasury's 4-week bill sale cleared at a high yield of 3.91%, compared with 3.945% at the previous auction. Bid-to-cover was 3.1, up from 2.820, and 16.96% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

squawks.headline: ECB policymakers see a December rate hike followed by a pause, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources say new ECB staff estimates show the rise in bond yields reducing growth by a cumulative 100bp and inflation by 90bp over 2027-28 compared with the September baseline.

squawks.headline: Cheniere says Europe needs an extra 69 million tonnes of LNG this winter and will have to draw cargoes away from Asia
squawks.detail: Cheniere's chief commercial officer, Anatol Feygin, said Europe will need an additional 69 million metric tons of LNG over the coming winter. He said the region will have to pull cargoes from Asia to meet it.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey pledges to set out benefit cuts before the end of this year
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the Chancellor made the commitment while answering criticism that Wednesday's Budget relies on unrealistic spending assumptions.

squawks.headline: IMF backs Fed Chair Warsh's focus on price stability
squawks.detail: The IMF said it fully supports Fed Chair Warsh's comments on focusing on price stability and that the Fed is right to watch the data closely.

squawks.headline: Trump weighs further military strikes on Iran after the midterms but is open to more diplomacy, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that President Trump is seriously considering more military operations against Iran after the US election while appearing willing to give diplomacy another chance. The report says many inside the administration doubt the case for resuming strikes.

squawks.headline: Netherlands releases its final 700K barrels of oil products to the market
squawks.detail: The Netherlands is releasing a last tranche of 700K barrels of oil products from its stocks to the market, according to a market newswire report.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says October CPI and PCE figures should show the Fed what action to take
squawks.detail: White House economic adviser Hassett said the October consumer price and PCE inflation data should make the appropriate Fed policy response clear.

squawks.headline: Greek PM Mitsotakis calls for an urgent global maritime truce and says attacks on commercial shipping are unacceptable
squawks.detail: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis said targeting civilian commercial shipping is unacceptable and that a global maritime truce is urgently needed.

squawks.headline: Iran has received a letter from US Vice President Vance but has not replied, and still insists on its seven conditions, Tasnim says
squawks.detail: Iran's Tasnim news agency reports that Tehran has received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance and has not yet responded. Tasnim says Iran is holding to its seven conditions for the US and will not accept any position that contradicts them.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says the Fed would probably act if October inflation comes in very high
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said the Federal Reserve would likely respond if October inflation proves very high. He made the remarks in a live appearance on 29 October.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says ECB business will continue with full continuity ahead of her departure
squawks.detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said the central bank will carry on its work with complete continuity. She said this after confirming she will step down on 7 February.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says ECB QT continues mechanically with no plan to change, and she is leaving early to speak freely on non-monetary issues
squawks.detail: At her post-decision press conference, ECB President Lagarde said the approach to bond repayments under quantitative tightening is unchanged and there is no plan to readjust it. She also said she is stepping down early so that she has freedom of expression on matters other than monetary policy.

squawks.headline: FT reports Hernández de Cos and Knot are frontrunners to succeed Lagarde as ECB President
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot lead the race to become the ECB's fifth president, after Lagarde confirmed she will step down on 7 February.

squawks.headline: QatarEnergy aims to lift outside LNG purchases well beyond 7 million tonnes a year by end-2026
squawks.detail: QatarEnergy is reported to be securing long-term LNG supplies from the US and elsewhere to hedge against future Hormuz disruption, and plans to expand those purchases to well beyond 7 million tonnes a year by the end of 2026.

squawks.headline: OBR cuts its five-year housing delivery forecast by 190,000 homes, citing weak demand and rising costs
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility expects 190,000 fewer homes to be delivered over the next five years than in its March 2026 forecast, Inside Housing reports.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says the ECB's direction of travel on rates is clear barring a surprise and it has tools for transmission disruptions
squawks.detail: Speaking at the ECB press conference, President Lagarde also said there is no plan to limit the number of meetings.

squawks.headline: QatarEnergy CEO says two LNG trains hit in Iranian attacks need about three years to repair, cutting capacity by 17% meanwhile
squawks.detail: The QatarEnergy chief executive said full LNG output could restart within a week of a peace deal if ships are available, that Pearl GTL is due back by Q1 2027, and that the 142 MTPA expansion plan is unchanged. He also said LNG from new purchase agreements cannot be offered to long-term customers as a Hormuz backup.

squawks.headline: QatarEnergy CEO says it is buying US LNG to hedge against future Hormuz disruption and rules out bypass pipelines
squawks.detail: The QatarEnergy chief executive said the company expects to sign more long-term LNG purchase deals with the US and other suppliers by the end of 2026, aiming for well above 7 million tonnes a year. He said pipelines that bypass Hormuz are ruled out because any infrastructure in the region could be targeted.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says long-end yields have risen worldwide and high-debt countries must plan for rates staying higher
squawks.detail: At her press conference, ECB President Lagarde said the ECB is watching the 10-year and the whole bond curve, and that borrowing by hyperscalers is one reason yields have risen. She also said the ECB will probably prepare scenarios in December.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says ECB Governing Council discussed whether a rate rise would be appropriate but kept its measured approach
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said at the post-decision press conference that the Governing Council debated a hike, but that a measured approach is still suitable for now. She said the ECB is unanimously seen as well positioned and strong enough to wait for further data.

squawks.headline: Budget changes how self-assessment income taxpayers make payments on account
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey confirmed in the Autumn Budget that the government will change how income tax self-assessment taxpayers make their advance payments on account, City AM reports. Tax advisers have raised concerns about the effect on cash flow for the self-employed.

squawks.headline: Lagarde sees no material risk of second-round inflation effects now, though indirect energy price effects have intensified
squawks.detail: At her post-decision press conference, ECB President Lagarde said she sees no sign of second-round effects beyond the ECB's projections, although the indirect impact of the energy price surge has intensified. She also said long-term borrowing costs have risen since September.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says eurozone growth risks are to the downside and inflation risks to the upside, with financial conditions tighter
squawks.detail: At the ECB press conference, President Lagarde said financial conditions have tightened since the last meeting. She added that fiscal uncertainty and weaker market sentiment could tighten financing conditions further and dampen demand.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says ECB wage tracker points to 2.5%-2.8% growth for rest of 2026 and energy prices have risen beyond baseline
squawks.detail: At the ECB press conference, Lagarde said underlying inflation stayed largely steady, early stages of the pricing chain show upward pressure, wage pressures are moderate and most long-term inflation expectation gauges are near 2%. She said AI investment and public spending should support growth, and that fiscal measures should be temporary, focused and tailored.

squawks.headline: Lagarde says the eurozone economy expanded in Q3 and growth stays supported, but higher energy prices hurt consumer confidence
squawks.detail: At her press conference after the ECB's decision to hold rates, President Lagarde said incoming data show the economy grew in the third quarter and that growth should remain supported in the near term. She said the new rise in energy prices is weighing on consumer confidence.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says Trump believes rates can be lower but respects Fed independence
squawks.detail: Speaking to Fox Business, Hassett said inflation came in close to expectations, that GDP is moving towards 4% growth and that a supply-side boom is pushing prices down. He said Trump thinks rates can be lower and respects the Fed's independence.

squawks.headline: France lowers diesel stockholding requirements to release supply
squawks.detail: A French official said the government has reduced the mandatory diesel stocks it requires so that more supply can reach the market.

squawks.headline: UK September mortgage approvals are the lowest since December 2023; unsecured lending growth is the fastest since 2018
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that lenders approved the fewest mortgages since December 2023 last month as borrowing costs rose. Unsecured lending to households grew at its fastest annual pace since 2018.

squawks.headline: Treasury lowers its 2031-32 day-to-day spending assumption by £5.5bn in Budget plans
squawks.detail: An economics journalist reports that the Treasury trimmed its assumption for day-to-day departmental spending in 2031-32 by £5.5bn. No department yet has a budget set for that year.

squawks.headline: French-German 10-year yield spread narrows 4bp to 150bp after ECB decision
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that the gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields tightened by 4bp to 150bp after the ECB's rate decision.

squawks.headline: BoE opens consultation on rules for central counterparties accepting tokenised collateral
squawks.detail: The Bank of England said on Thursday it is consulting on the requirements central counterparties must meet before they can accept tokenised collateral. The Bank said this could make margin calls and wider collateral management easier, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Euro falls 0.4% to $1.11095, its lowest since May 2025, as traders cut ECB hike pricing to 68bp by end-2027
squawks.detail: The euro slipped after the ECB's decision to hold rates and was last down 0.4% at $1.11095, its lowest since May 2025. Market pricing for ECB rate hikes was pared to 68bp by the end of 2027.

squawks.headline: ECB says a larger, longer energy shock is likely to push inflation up and growth down; keeps meeting-by-meeting approach
squawks.detail: The ECB's statement says energy prices have kept rising, posing upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth, while underlying inflation has stayed broadly stable and wages show no material response so far. It says financing conditions have tightened since the last meeting, it will not pre-commit to a rate path, and APP and PEPP holdings continue to shrink with no reinvestment.

squawks.headline: ECB holds rates as expected, with the deposit facility rate at 2.50% and the main refinancing rate at 2.65%
squawks.detail: The ECB kept its October policy rates unchanged. The deposit facility rate stays at 2.50% and the main refinancing rate at 2.65%, both in line with forecasts, including the Reuters poll.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says Britain is working to de-escalate and reopen the Strait of Hormuz fully, and to cut the welfare bill
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the UK is doing all it can to de-escalate and to support a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran must have no nuclear capability. On the same occasion he said the government is working to reduce the welfare bill as soon as possible.

squawks.headline: France's Macron thanks Lagarde and says the ECB leadership handover must be orderly and balanced, prepared with European partners
squawks.detail: French President Macron thanked Christine Lagarde after the ECB confirmed her resignation as President, effective 7 February. He said the transition at the top of the ECB should now be prepared with European partners in an orderly and balanced way.

squawks.headline: EUR/GBP falls to its lowest level since April 2025 as sterling firms against the euro
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported that the euro fell against sterling to its lowest level since April 2025. The post gave no exchange rate.

squawks.headline: US September PCE supercore inflation rises to 3.596% year on year from 3.493%; monthly pace at 0.367%
squawks.detail: US PCE supercore prices rose 3.596% on the year in September, up from 3.493% the previous month. The monthly rate was 0.367%, compared with 0.373% previously.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide warns large Ukrainian attacks over 4 November celebrations could shift Russia's stance on trilateral talks
squawks.detail: A Kremlin aide said, according to Interfax, that major Ukrainian attacks during the 4 November celebrations could affect Russia's attitude towards the trilateral negotiations on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says typical household energy bills this year are close to 2022-23 levels
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation said the typical UK household will pay nearly as much for energy this year as it did in 2022-23.

squawks.headline: PM Starmer's spokesman says Burnham and Healey both think the welfare bill needs to fall
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman said Burnham and Healey share the view that welfare spending should be reduced. This follows Healey's commitment to cut welfare spending before the next election, with plans due by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: US Q3 GDP price index rises 2.3%, below the 3.2% forecast; quarterly core PCE prices up 2.5%
squawks.detail: The US advance Q3 GDP report puts the GDP price index at 2.3% against a 3.2% forecast and 3.5% previously. Core PCE prices rose 2.5% against a 2.4% forecast and 3.3% previously, and headline PCE prices rose 2.1% after 5.0%.

squawks.headline: US September PCE prices rise 0.5% on the month and core 0.3%, both as forecast; core annual rate at 3.1%
squawks.detail: US data show headline PCE prices up 0.5% on the month (previous 0.3%) and core up 0.3% (previous 0.2%), both matching forecasts. Core PCE is 3.1% year on year against a 3.1% forecast; reports of the headline annual rate differ. Personal income rose 0.2% against a 0.3% forecast, spending rose 0.5% against 0.6%, and real consumption was flat against a 0.1% forecast.

squawks.headline: US initial jobless claims hold at 194K, below the 198K forecast
squawks.detail: US weekly initial jobless claims were 194K, unchanged from the previous week and below the forecast of 198K.

squawks.headline: US continuing jobless claims fall to 1.701M, below the 1.72M forecast
squawks.detail: US continuing jobless claims came in at 1.701M, down from 1.728M previously and below the 1.72M forecast.

squawks.headline: US Q3 GDP grows 3.4% in advance estimate, above the 3.2% consensus
squawks.detail: The advance estimate puts US third-quarter GDP growth at 3.4%, compared with a consensus of 3.2%.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says the search for Lagarde's successor at the ECB will be finished by the end of the year
squawks.detail: The German Chancellor said the process to choose the next ECB President will be completed by year-end. Lagarde's resignation takes effect on 7 February.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the forecast for the level of GDP in 2030 is unchanged after the Budget
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the GDP growth forecast picks up after a hit in the near term. It adds that other population assumptions make up for lower migration, so the 2030 level is unchanged.

squawks.headline: RBC analysts say NatWest, Nationwide and Lloyds take the biggest profit hit from the Budget's doubled bank surcharge
squawks.detail: City AM reports RBC analysts' view that UK-focused lenders are more exposed than HSBC and Barclays to the Budget's doubling of the bank surcharge.

squawks.headline: Budget shields low-income pensioners from income tax as state pension rises; report says some face a 53% effective rate
squawks.detail: City AM reports that new Budget rules from Chancellor Healey exempt low-income pensioners from income tax on the state pension. The report says hundreds of thousands of pensioners would pay an effective 53% rate on part of their retirement income.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says 2020s set to be the worst decade on record for real household disposable income growth
squawks.detail: In its post-Budget analysis 'Spread thin', the Resolution Foundation says real household disposable income will end the 2020s only 1.4% higher than at the start of the decade.

squawks.headline: Italian consumer confidence falls to 90.3, below the 91 forecast; manufacturing confidence holds at 91.9
squawks.detail: Italy's October consumer confidence came in at 90.3, against a forecast of 91 and down from 91.2 previously. Manufacturing business confidence was 91.9, the same as the previous reading and just below the 92 forecast.

squawks.headline: Lagarde resigned from the ECB because she could no longer stay neutral on French politics, a source says
squawks.detail: An unnamed source gave this as the reason for ECB President Lagarde's resignation, which takes effect on 7 February. The ECB had already formally confirmed that she is leaving.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the OBR forecast higher borrowing and debt than in March before Budget measures
squawks.detail: In its Budget analysis 'Spread thin', the Resolution Foundation says the OBR's pre-measures forecast had government borrowing and debt above its March projections. No figures were given in the post.

squawks.headline: IFS says Budget plans for public service spending are very tight and doubts the government will deliver them
squawks.detail: At its post-Budget briefing, the Institute for Fiscal Studies questioned whether defence spending can reach 3% of GDP entirely within existing spending envelopes. It also said repeated small changes from Budget to Budget have left the tax system overly complex.

squawks.headline: ECB formally confirms Lagarde has resigned as President, effective 7 February
squawks.detail: The European Central Bank said in a statement on Thursday that President Christine Lagarde has resigned and will leave on 7 February. This follows earlier reports that she had told staff of her plans.

squawks.headline: Healey says preventative spending will be ringfenced at the 2027 spending review
squawks.detail: According to the Institute for Government, John Healey has announced that the government will put a ringfence around preventative spending at the 2027 spending review.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says the target pump price for petrol will rise by 5 yen per litre each month from December
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the target petrol price will go up by 5 yen per litre each month from December into the spring. She also confirmed the decision to subsidise power and gas bills from December.

squawks.headline: EU's Costa says the search for Lagarde's successor as ECB President begins today and will go ahead without delay
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa said Lagarde had told him she intends to leave the ECB presidency on 7 February 2027. He said the appointment process for her successor starts today.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says subsidies to curb electricity and gas bills will run from December to February
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the government will introduce support measures for household electricity and gas bills starting in December and running until February.

squawks.headline: Lagarde's successor at the ECB is to be appointed by the European Council under the EU treaty nomination process
squawks.detail: The European Council will appoint the next ECB President using the nomination procedure in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This follows Lagarde telling staff she plans to step down on 7 February.

squawks.headline: ECB President Lagarde tells staff she plans to step down on 7 February
squawks.detail: Reports on 29 October say ECB President Christine Lagarde has told staff she intends to leave her post on 7 February. The reports give no reason for her departure and name no successor.

squawks.headline: Haskel says ONS productivity revisions came too late for the OBR forecast; OBR raised total factor productivity for AI
squawks.detail: Speaking at a Resolution Foundation event, former MPC member Jonathan Haskel said recent ONS revisions that lift output per hour arrived too late to go into the OBR forecast and do not change the outlook for productivity growth. He noted that the OBR raised its total factor productivity assumption because of the effect of AI.

squawks.headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to 53.4K in September, below the 54K forecast; M4 money supply grows 0.1% on the month
squawks.detail: Bank of England data put September mortgage approvals at 53.443K against a forecast of 54K, with August revised to 54.814K. M4 money supply rose 0.1% on the month and 3.9% on the year, down from 4.4%, and M4 excluding intermediate OFCs grew at a 1.6% three-month annualised rate, down from 2.8%.

squawks.headline: UK consumer credit rises £1.914bn and mortgage lending £3.866bn, both below forecasts, BoE data show
squawks.detail: Bank of England figures show consumer credit of £1.914bn against a £2bn forecast and £2.464bn previously. Net mortgage lending was £3.866bn against a £4.2bn forecast, with the previous month revised to £4.174bn from £4.410bn.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield falls 3bp to 5.29%, a five-week low
squawks.detail: The benchmark 10-year gilt yield fell 3bp to 5.29% in morning trading, its lowest level in five weeks.

squawks.headline: Italian unemployment rate rises to 6.3%, above the 6.2% forecast
squawks.detail: Italy's unemployment rate came in at 6.3%, against a forecast of 6.2% and a previous reading of 6.2%.

squawks.headline: Trump administration is in continuing talks on a temporary peace deal, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the US administration is in ongoing talks on a temporary peace deal. The report did not say which conflict the talks cover.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says three oil tankers hit mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian reports cite the IRGC navy as saying three tankers caught fire after hitting mines over the past 24 hours while using an unauthorised route off the southern side of the strait. US CENTCOM had earlier rejected Iranian media claims of ships hitting mines and said main transit routes had been cleared.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco sets its November butane price at $780 a tonne
squawks.detail: Saudi Aramco has set its contract price for November butane at $780 per tonne, according to a market wire headline.

squawks.headline: EU energy commissioner says the threat to jet fuel supply security seen this summer has passed
squawks.detail: The EU's energy chief said there had been a risk to the security of jet fuel supply this summer and that the risk is no longer present.

squawks.headline: Lloyds Q3 pre-tax profit rises nearly 99% to £2.3bn as costs fall and there are no major impairment charges
squawks.detail: Lloyds Banking Group reported third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.3bn, ahead of expectations. City AM said the rise came from a lower cost base and the absence of any major impairment charges.

squawks.headline: EU energy commissioner says the bloc uses 18% less gas than in 2022 and is better placed for the current crisis
squawks.detail: The EU energy commissioner said the bloc is better able to handle the current energy crisis than in 2022 because gas use is 18% lower. The commissioner also said the crisis is made worse by its impact on oil products.

squawks.headline: South Korea sets November treasury bond issuance at 12tn won
squawks.detail: South Korea will issue 12tn won of treasury bonds in November. The finance minister had earlier said Seoul would review November issuance in response to market turbulence.

squawks.headline: India's trade minister says the US trade deal will protect farmers and all stakeholders and leave India at a strong comparative advantage
squawks.detail: India's trade minister said that no sensitive interest of farmers or any other stakeholder would be compromised by the planned trade deal with the US. He added that India would hold a strong comparative advantage once the deal is completed.

squawks.headline: Lloyds Q3 net interest income comes in at £3.81bn, just below the £3.83bn estimate
squawks.detail: Lloyds reported Q3 2026 loan-loss provisions of £313.0m (estimate £311.8m) and operating costs of £2.37bn (estimate £2.39bn). Total deposits were £502.8bn, against an estimate of £502.41bn.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry says it will take all necessary measures if the EU imposes discriminatory restrictions on Chinese goods
squawks.detail: China's Ministry of Commerce issued the warning about any EU curbs on Chinese products on 29 October. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Healey commits to cutting welfare spending before the next election, with plans due by the end of the year
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor, having delivered her first Budget, has promised to publish plans by the end of the year to reduce a welfare bill she called unsustainable.

squawks.headline: Swedish Q3 GDP rises 0.4% on the quarter, above the 0.3% forecast; September GDP indicator falls 0.7% on the month
squawks.detail: Sweden's Q3 GDP indicator rose 0.4% quarter on quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and 1.4% previously. The monthly indicator for September fell 0.7% after a 1.1% rise, and its annual rate slowed to 2.1% from 3.5%.

squawks.headline: Swedish retail sales fall 0.4% in September and consumer confidence drops to 94.3 in October
squawks.detail: Swedish retail sales fell 0.4% month on month in September after a revised 0.9% rise, and annual growth slowed to 5.5% from a revised 7.2%. Consumer confidence fell to 94.3 in October from 102.2, while manufacturing confidence rose to 111.5 from 106.3.

squawks.headline: Swedish GDP growth slows to 2.8% year on year in advance estimate, just below the 2.9% forecast
squawks.detail: Sweden's advance GDP estimate showed annual growth of 2.8%, against a forecast of 2.9% and down from 3.3% previously.

squawks.headline: China opposes US move to put Chinese firms on a Xinjiang-related entity list and vows to protect its interests
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said the US listing of Chinese companies goes against the consensus reached by the two heads of state. It called on Washington to stop immediately and said China will take the steps needed to protect its interests.

squawks.headline: Bank of Korea board member Hwang says it is time to focus on inflation and the won is moving faster than expected
squawks.detail: Hwang said the Bank of Korea is watching the FX market closely and that high borrowing costs are limiting gains for small and medium firms. He cited an upward revision to the 2026 current account surplus to $500bn from $450bn.

squawks.headline: Budget scorecard assumes approval of North Sea discovery drilling producing more than a billion barrels
squawks.detail: City AM reports that the Budget scorecard assumes the government will approve North Sea discovery drilling projects producing over a billion barrels of oil and gas, following Jackdaw and Rosebank.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield falls 5bp to 5.311% in Asian trading
squawks.detail: The long bond yield fell 5 basis points to 5.311% during Asian hours on Thursday, while US equity futures sold off.

squawks.headline: China's onshore yuan strengthens to 6.6621 per dollar, its strongest since 7 June 2022
squawks.detail: The onshore yuan rose to 6.6621 per US dollar in Asian trading on Thursday, its strongest level since 7 June 2022.

squawks.headline: RBNZ Governor Breman says the chance of a December rate hike is high
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman said on Thursday that the likelihood of the bank raising the official cash rate in December is high.

squawks.headline: JGB yields rise ahead of the BoJ policy announcement, with the 5-year up 1.5bp at 2.28%
squawks.detail: The 5-year Japanese government bond yield rose 1.5bp to 2.28% as investors waited for the Bank of Japan's policy decision, WSJ reported.

squawks.headline: South Korea's finance minister says Seoul will act promptly on market turbulence and review November bond issuance
squawks.detail: South Korea's finance minister said the government will respond quickly to any jump in market volatility, will carefully assess the size of November treasury bond issuance and will buy back treasury bonds if needed.

squawks.headline: BoC's Macklem says Canada's neutral rate estimate could rise and the inflation forecast assumes fuel costs pass through
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said the estimate of the neutral interest rate may be revised up and the bank's inflation forecast rests on fuel costs passing through to prices. He added that a new model lets the bank break inflation down by component, and described earlier core CPI forecasts as a shortcut.

squawks.headline: Hong Kong Monetary Authority leaves its base rate at 4.25%
squawks.detail: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority kept its base rate unchanged at 4.25% after the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates.

squawks.headline: Trump says he did not instruct Vance to write to Iran
squawks.detail: President Trump said he had not told Vice President Vance to send the letter to Iran. The WSJ had reported that Vance wrote to a senior Iranian hard-liner to try to restart peace talks.

squawks.headline: Fitch says US fiscal pressures will persist whatever the midterm election result
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings said pressure on US public finances is set to continue regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections. The post reported no rating action.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says timing of Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine depends partly on the battlefield situation
squawks.detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said the date for the negotiations in Abu Dhabi will depend on factors including the situation on the battlefield and the wider situation. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Budget confirms £1.5bn of devolved loans for mayoral authorities plus extra funding for social housing and rough sleeping
squawks.detail: Inside Housing reports that the Chancellor's Budget repeats the Prime Minister's earlier announcement giving mayoral authorities access to £1.5bn of devolved loans. The Budget also confirms more funding for the Social and Affordable Homes Programme and for rough sleeping.

squawks.headline: Bessent says US trade deals are largely locked in and consumer and business behaviour is strong
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC that much of Trump's economic agenda, including tax cuts, is already in place, and that the trade deals are mostly locked in. He also said France has a tough hand. His CNBC appearance has now ended.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK plans a much larger fiscal consolidation than other high-income OECD countries
squawks.detail: In its post-Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation said the government's planned fiscal consolidation is much bigger than those of other high-income OECD countries. It added that it is not yet clear whether the plans will be delivered.

squawks.headline: Global bond sales hit an annual record of $6.61 trillion
squawks.detail: Market reports on 28 October said global bond issuance this year has reached a record $6.61 trillion.

squawks.headline: Bessent says the Iran operation is working and Tehran is cut off from dollars; sees no problem in AI-related borrowing
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Operation Outcast on Iran is succeeding, that Iran cannot get dollars and that funding for its proxies is falling. He also said he does not regard AI borrowing or wider spreads on AI-issuer debt as a problem, and described France as having a tough hand.

squawks.headline: Bessent says US faces an energy supply shock and the Fed should keep an open mind; says bonds have done much of the tightening
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said he expects a strong US third-quarter GDP figure, that the Fed is very attentive to inflation having been above target for a long time, and that yields and oil prices are closely correlated. He also said he and Trump have a lot of confidence in Fed Chair Warsh.

squawks.headline: Trump signs proclamation on US imports of robotics and industrial machinery but imposes no immediate tariffs
squawks.detail: The White House says President Trump has signed a proclamation adjusting US imports of robotics, industrial machinery and their parts and components. It says these imports pose national security risks, but no tariffs take effect immediately.

squawks.headline: Germany will let offshore wind developers hand back auctioned sites if they pay a penalty
squawks.detail: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said on Wednesday that companies may return offshore wind sites they won at auction, as long as they pay a penalty to the transmission system operators. Reuters reports that the sector is under growing economic pressure.

squawks.headline: US Vice President Vance writes to a senior Iranian hard-liner in an attempt to restart peace talks, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The WSJ reports that Vance sent the letter to the secretary of Iran's top security body, a former long-serving IRGC commander. One person said the letter was sent at Trump's direction and that Trump knows about the continuing outreach.

squawks.headline: US proposal reportedly combines Iran's seven conditions with US nuclear demands in phases; Iran wants its conditions met first
squawks.detail: An Al Jazeera reporter says the US proposal pairs Iran's seven conditions with US demands on highly enriched uranium and inspections, to be implemented in phases. The reporter says Iran insists its conditions are met before any nuclear negotiations, while indirect US-Iran messages continue.

squawks.headline: Healey asks BoE to review banks' capital requirements and says the bank tax rise will have a time limit in law
squawks.detail: In post-Budget remarks, Chancellor Healey said she has asked the Bank of England to look at banks' capital requirements and that legislation for the higher bank tax will include a time limit. She also said the government will press ahead with the financial services and markets bill and that business costs were a Budget priority.

squawks.headline: Iran proposal also covers lifting the blockade, the nuclear issue and the return of inspectors, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya reports that the schedule of the new proposal under discussion with Iran covers reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the blockade, dealing with Iran's nuclear programme and calling in inspectors. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM rejects Iranian media claims that commercial ships are hitting sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US Central Command said claims carried by Iranian-controlled media in recent days and weeks, that commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were striking sea mines, are false.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy acknowledges for the first time that Russia needs security guarantees, as US-led peace diplomacy picks up
squawks.detail: The Ukrainian president acknowledged Russia's need for security guarantees, a change in Kyiv's position. He said ending the war and securing Ukraine must still come first.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM says US forces have cleared sea mines from the main transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US Central Command says all internationally recognised primary transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared of sea mines by US forces and remain clear. It says thousands of commercial vessels have used the lanes safely and are still using them today.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR sees UK welfare bill rising by £38bn by 2031-32 while reform waits on reviews
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the OBR expects welfare spending to increase by £38bn by 2031-32, led by the State Pension and by health and disability benefits for people of working age. It says welfare reform is paused until the Milburn and Timms reviews report.

squawks.headline: Iran and mediators weigh Turkey meeting before 4 November on new proposal covering Hormuz reopening, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, says Iran and mediators are discussing a meeting in Turkey before 4 November. It says the timeline in the new proposal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the siege.

squawks.headline: Warsh ends press conference saying he is comfortable with the Fed tightening financial conditions; Fed not involved in Cook proceedings
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said tighter financial conditions show that policy is working and that he is not uncomfortable with them. Asked about the proceedings involving Governor Cook, he said the Fed is not involved as far as he knows, and then ended the press conference.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 4.11bp to 5.034% during Warsh's press conference
squawks.detail: The 10-year Treasury note yield was last reported up 4.11bp at 5.034% while Fed Chair Warsh was speaking after the Fed's decision to hold rates.

squawks.headline: Warsh says balance sheet task force will report to the FOMC early in Q1 and most Fed colleagues do not see the economy running too hot
squawks.detail: Fed Chair Warsh said any balance sheet changes would follow serious consideration of the task force's recommendations and are unlikely to affect the current policy juncture. He also said productivity has been rising, higher growth does not mean it is causing inflation, and he does not think the Fed has to throw people out of work.

squawks.headline: Warsh says he will not give forward guidance outside a crisis or prejudge December, and that politics played no part in the decision
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed may learn a lot before December and that neither the midterm elections nor politics came up in FOMC deliberations. He also said rates have affected investment inside and outside the technology sector since early September, that capex strength has broadened, that credit spreads have widened for some assets, and that he has noted the rise in oil futures.

squawks.headline: Warsh says the Fed's 2% PCE goal is not a soft target and longer-term inflation expectations remain anchored
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said near-term inflation expectations have risen but longer-term measures still show confidence in price stability. He called the FOMC meeting a family fight that reached the right decision, and said market interest rates have turned lower despite a usually stable link with rising oil prices.

squawks.headline: Warsh says swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and the Fed removed some accommodation in September
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the period ahead would bring plenty of information and he was comfortable with the signposts. He added that the conclusions of the Fed's five task forces are unlikely to feed into policy at this point, and that he may speak at a task force field hearing on 16 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Warsh says tightening is starting to work and credit conditions have tightened, but he will not call financial conditions tight
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed removed some accommodation in September, that swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and that he is not surprised by market volatility. He said the committee is focused mainly on price stability, will not tolerate inflation above the 2% target, and that the period ahead is rich in information.

squawks.headline: Warsh says the Fed will change its FOMC schedule, with one 2027 meeting lacking a rate vote and 6 policy-setting meetings expected in 2028
squawks.detail: At his press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed will keep 8 meetings a year, with one focused on strategy and one with no rate vote or statement in 2027, and two without a rate vote in 2028. He also said the Fed has shown it is willing and ready to act, that growth has strengthened and credit conditions have tightened, and that he would not call financial conditions tight.

squawks.headline: WTI December crude settles up 2.88% at $102.78 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December futures settled $2.88 higher at $102.78 a barrel on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Fed Chair Warsh says inflation remains elevated and the Fed has not grown easier; sees 3Q US GDP likely above 3%
squawks.detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said economic activity is expanding strongly, business investment is likely rising at a double-digit pace and the committee wants more information to set the policy stance. He said the Fed's responsibility is to get inflation down and that he is not surprised by market volatility.
